notes: Four separate Linux processes; default allocator; 500,000 entries in one directory; synthetic metadata without FUSE, network or credentials.
Fixture construction uses bounded 1,000-entry pages. Snapshot representation is populated with SQL so a large foreground input vector does not contaminate the baseline.
Both variants use the new schema and ordered SQL. This compares visitor retention with the compatibility collector, not old and new implementations.
Foreground network publication, Engine/FUSE projection, open directory snapshots, namespace byte budgets and long-session memory remain outside this fixture.
Database bytes include reusable pages left by staging; they are not live entry payload bytes or an end-to-end disk quota measurement.
Stream checks bound additional read RSS/high-water growth to 64 MiB. Constant sampled RSS here is not a universal whole-process memory guarantee.
